conflict.title: Institutional strength and democratic integrity
conflict.summary: A cooperative needs enough capacity to survive, but concentrating authority to get it erodes the member control that made it worth building.

conflict.title: AI capability and resilient autonomy
conflict.summary: A community may need AI to keep up with rivals who use it, yet its essential functions must keep working when AI, power or a provider fails.

conflict.title: Unilateral protection and common security
conflict.summary: Deterrence seems to demand more of a contested capability, while shared survival demands reciprocal limits on that same capability.

conflict.title: Present provision and ecological viability
conflict.summary: Essential services seem to depend on growing material throughput, while ecological limits require constraining it.

conflict.title: Controlled engagement and trustworthy relationships
conflict.summary: A service needs funding to last, but engineering people’s attachment to secure it undermines the free choice that trust depends on.

nodes.text: Humane institutions can survive and spread while retaining autonomy and care, within ecological limits and without catastrophic destruction.
nodes.label: Humane institutions survive and spread while retaining autonomy and care within liveable limits.

nodes.text: Communities can maintain useful material and organisational capabilities at viable cost.
nodes.label: Communities maintain useful capabilities at viable cost.

nodes.text: Members retain substantive control, justified trust and meaningful freedom to disagree or leave.
nodes.label: Members retain control, justified trust and freedom to disagree or leave.

nodes.text: Ecological and catastrophic risks remain compatible with continued human life and collective agency.
nodes.label: Ecological and catastrophic risks remain compatible with continued human agency.

backlog.label: Check this proposed common ground with the people in the discussion.
backlog.note: The supplied analyses report apparent agreements. None is recorded here as accepted; compare the original posts before inviting participants to review the wording.

backlog.label: Define realised progress, including survival and retention of the mission.
backlog.note: The first analysis proposes adoption retained in practice, with viability and faithfulness measured separately. Agree a bounded system, period and observable outcome rather than equating publications, satisfaction or market growth with success.

backlog.label: Review the wider programme before choosing further branches.
backlog.note: The second analysis also covers reflective development, the Laboratory, Forge/model adaptation, Vocal Presence, federation, material and energy services, and enforceable security. Its spiritual root is a philosophical hypothesis. This compact map does not establish a single global constraint or make the pilot the whole programme.

nodes.text: As a group grows, damaging disagreements can exceed members’ current conflict-handling capacity.
nodes.label: Damaging disagreements can exceed a growing group's current conflict-handling capacity.

nodes.text: The group needs workable coordination to remain viable.
nodes.label: The group needs workable coordination to remain viable.

nodes.text: When members cannot resolve damaging disagreements, central intervention may become the practical response.
nodes.label: Unresolved damaging disagreements may make central intervention the practical response.

assumptions.text: Conflict-handling capacity is insufficient for the selected function, and effective member-controlled alternatives are not already available.

backlog.label: Test whether conflict capacity limits this particular group's next achievement.
backlog.note: Compare developmental capacity, coordination design, resources and external pressures. A reported historical mechanism is not a measured constraint at a selected host.

nodes.text: Sustain an effective emancipatory institution.
nodes.label: Sustain an effective emancipatory institution.

nodes.text: Acquire enough coordination, expertise and resources to remain viable.
nodes.label: Acquire enough coordination, expertise and resources to remain viable.

nodes.text: Preserve substantive member control and the institution’s emancipatory purpose.
nodes.label: Preserve substantive member control and the institution’s emancipatory purpose.

nodes.text: Concentrate decision authority to obtain the required effectiveness.
nodes.label: Concentrate decision authority to obtain the required effectiveness.

nodes.text: Keep that same authority distributed among members.
nodes.label: Keep that same authority distributed among members.

nodes.text: Keep a community capable, independent and resilient.
nodes.label: Keep a community capable, independent and resilient.

nodes.text: Avoid being outperformed or subordinated by actors using advanced AI.
nodes.label: Avoid being outperformed or subordinated by actors using advanced AI.

nodes.text: Continue essential functions under provider, energy or AI failure.
nodes.label: Continue essential functions under provider, energy or AI failure.

nodes.text: Make the selected essential function depend on AI.
nodes.label: Make the selected essential function depend on AI.

nodes.text: Keep that same essential function operable without AI.
nodes.label: Keep that same essential function operable without AI.

nodes.text: Protect people’s rights and durable security.
nodes.label: Protect people’s rights and durable security.

nodes.text: Prevent coercion, attack or exploitation of restraint.
nodes.label: Prevent coercion, attack or exploitation of restraint.

nodes.text: Reduce escalation and collective exposure to catastrophic weapons.
nodes.label: Reduce escalation and collective exposure to catastrophic weapons.

nodes.text: Continue expanding the contested military capability to deter rivals.
nodes.label: Continue expanding the contested military capability to deter rivals.

nodes.text: Restrain expansion of that same capability through reciprocal limits.
nodes.label: Restrain expansion of that same capability through reciprocal limits.

nodes.text: Sustain human flourishing and essential services over time.
nodes.label: Sustain human flourishing and essential services over time.

nodes.text: Maintain livelihoods and services under existing economic dependencies.
nodes.label: Maintain livelihoods and services under existing economic dependencies.

nodes.text: Keep material demand and ecological damage within viable conditions.
nodes.label: Keep material demand and ecological damage within viable conditions.

nodes.text: Increase material throughput to maintain those services and commitments.
nodes.label: Increase material throughput to maintain those services and commitments.

nodes.text: Constrain that same throughput to protect their ecological basis.
nodes.label: Constrain that same throughput to protect their ecological basis.

nodes.text: Provide a durable service that genuinely supports human agency.
nodes.label: Provide a durable service that genuinely supports human agency.

nodes.text: Secure the resources and continuity needed to maintain the service.
nodes.label: Secure the resources and continuity needed to maintain the service.

nodes.text: Protect truthful inquiry, voluntary participation and non-instrumental care.
nodes.label: Protect truthful inquiry, voluntary participation and non-instrumental care.

nodes.text: Engineer attachment and user responses to secure the provider’s required returns.
nodes.label: Engineer attachment and user responses to secure the provider’s required returns.

nodes.text: Allow those same responses to remain freely chosen, including disagreement or exit.
nodes.label: Allow those same responses to remain freely chosen, including disagreement or exit.

assumptions.text: The required coordination and expertise are obtainable only, or at substantially lower viable cost, through concentrated authority.
Members cannot retain substantive control if those decisions are transferred to managers or central bodies.

source_refs.locator: p. 14, K1, C to D prime

assumptions.text: The same decisions at the same scale and time must be either centrally controlled or genuinely controlled by members; no workable division or accountable delegation is available.

source_refs.locator: p. 14, K1, D conflicts with D prime

assumptions.text: AI provides a decisive advantage for this function, and a non-AI or optional-AI arrangement cannot meet the requirement.
AI access cannot be made sufficiently dependable, locally controlled and replaceable for the selected essential function.

source_refs.locator: p. 15, K2, C to D prime

assumptions.text: No tested fallback, bounded role or diversified architecture can reconcile these requirements for the same function at the same time.

source_refs.locator: p. 15, K2, D conflicts with D prime

assumptions.text: Superior or matching relative destructive capacity is the only credible protection.
Unchecked competitive accumulation increases mutual insecurity.

source_refs.locator: p. 16, K3, C to D prime

assumptions.text: Reciprocal restraints cannot be verified, enforced or maintained against powerful defectors while protecting weaker parties.

source_refs.locator: p. 16, K3, D conflicts with D prime

assumptions.text: Services, employment, finance or welfare commitments cannot remain viable without continued material expansion.
Demand and impacts exceed the relevant ecological limits; efficiency alone does not control total demand.

source_refs.locator: p. 17, K4, C to D prime

assumptions.text: Service redesign, distributional changes, sufficiency and alternative energy or material configurations cannot meet needs within the limits in time.

source_refs.locator: p. 17, K4, D conflicts with D prime

assumptions.text: Financial or institutional continuity requires manipulating engagement, attachment or compliance.
Justified and generative trust require meaningful agency and correction, rather than manufactured confidence alone.

source_refs.locator: p. 18, K5, C to D prime

assumptions.text: No funding, ownership or accountability arrangement can sustain the service through benefits people can freely recognise and choose.

source_refs.locator: p. 18, K5, D conflicts with D prime

backlog.label: Can coordination and expertise be had without concentrating authority?
backlog.note: The analysis names conflict guidance, local AI, federation and accountable governance as candidate ways through. Leif hopes widely available conflict competence could reduce reliance on hierarchical intervention; none of these routes has been tested.

source_refs.locator: p. 14, K1, candidate injections I02, I03, I06 and I10

backlog.label: Does this function actually require AI to remain viable?
backlog.note: Leif argues that communities may have no viable alternative to building AI in; Robert holds that relying on AI as a core social technology is asking for trouble, and Leif has asked him to say where he places that limit. Keep non-AI and optional-AI comparators. Neither has reviewed this wording.

backlog.label: Test an exit and a fallback before treating AI dependence as unavoidable.
Can reciprocal limits be enforced against powerful defectors?
backlog.note: Leif asks why the League of Nations and the United Nations failed to prevent major wars, and what would make rules hold when powerful actors find them inconvenient. Robert expects the arms race may worsen before it improves, and looks to a coalition of middle powers for leverage.

backlog.label: Can essential services be kept without growing material throughput?
backlog.note: Leif hopes AI can speed up the development of alternative energy and materials. Robert prefers Nate Hagens’s Great Simplification and hedging against bets on AI. Both are candidate ways through; neither has been tested.

backlog.label: Can a service be funded without engineering attachment?
backlog.note: Leif’s essay contrasts institutions that earn trust with those that depend on manipulation. Robert accepts AI only if people stay free to take it or leave it.

nodes.text: Test member-controlled AI conflict guidance with voluntary use, human support, a workable exit and competence checked without AI.
nodes.label: Test voluntary, member-controlled AI conflict guidance with an exit and independent competence.

source_refs.locator: pp. 18–19, I02 and I03; p. 42, T2 and T3

nodes.text: Members establish confidentiality, fair grievance handling and independent comparison before live use.
nodes.label: Members establish confidentiality, fair grievance handling and independent comparison.

nodes.text: Destructive conflict costs and unnecessary hierarchical intervention fall while fair treatment, independent competence and member influence are retained.
nodes.label: Conflict costs and needless hierarchy fall while fair treatment, competence and influence remain.

nodes.text: Conflict guidance may suppress justified grievances even when satisfaction improves.
nodes.label: Conflict guidance may suppress justified grievances even when satisfaction improves.

source_refs.locator: p. 42, T2 defeating results and protected conditions

assumptions.text: The guidance fits the selected workflow, protections operate in practice, and observed gains exceed those from attention or ordinary human facilitation alone.

source_refs.locator: p. 42, T2; combined trial design is an AI reconstruction

assumptions.text: The risk arises where guidance privileges agreement or management expectations over substantive fairness; it is not an inevitable effect of guidance.

source_refs.locator: p. 42, T2; risk route reconstructed from the cautions

backlog.label: Compare AI guidance with optional-AI and human approaches.
backlog.note: Check useful output, total cost, energy, member control, fallback and competence without the tool. Participants have not committed to running this comparison.

backlog.label: Decide in advance what evidence would change the hypothesis.
backlog.note: Lower satisfaction scores or fewer complaints alone do not establish benefit. The first analysis asks whether small democratic groups gain more than hierarchies; the second distinguishes local improvements from the still-unclosed institutional-selection claim F17. One successful pilot cannot establish the larger claim.

backlog.label: Assess suppressed grievances separately from satisfaction.
backlog.note: Retain independent human support and a way to report costs, unfairness, dependency and increased concentration of authority.

nodes.text: A bounded comparative trial produces reviewable observations of benefits, harms, costs and decision rights.
nodes.label: A bounded comparative trial produces reviewable observations of benefits, harms and control.

nodes.text: A willing host and one function are selected, with the actual workflow and resource requirements documented.
nodes.label: Select a willing host and one function, with actual workflow and resource needs documented.

nodes.text: Affected people authorise a trial specification covering comparisons, measures, protections, responsibilities, resources and fallback.
nodes.label: Affected people authorise a comparative trial with measures, protections, resources and fallback.

nodes.text: The supplied record does not establish a confirmed operational case and authorised trial specification.
nodes.label: The supplied record does not establish a confirmed case and authorised trial specification.

source_refs.locator: p. 35, P01; p. 48, acceptance, baseline and next achievement

backlog.label: Verify the actual host's obstacles rather than assuming missing details are missing capacity.
backlog.note: The PDF distinguishes documented gaps, source-defined risks, reconstructed requirements and conditions to check locally (D/S/R/X). This statement concerns evidence in the supplied record, not proof that no willing host or resources exist.

backlog.label: Agree measures, responsibilities, resources and a person who can assess the outcomes.
backlog.note: No owner, budget, baseline, target, date or feedback commitment is assigned here. A trial is not ready until the affected people confirm these conditions. Future benefit and harm feedback should preserve both original expectations.

nodes.text: Select one willing host and one function, and confirm what is already operating.
nodes.label: Select one willing host and one function, and confirm what is already operating.

nodes.text: The bounded case and its factual starting conditions are documented.
nodes.label: The bounded case and its factual starting conditions are documented.

backlog.label: Ask who wants to take responsibility for selecting the first case.
backlog.note: This is a proposed action, not an invitation already sent or a commitment by Leif, Robert or any cooperative.
